status_summary: On the election item, a Secretary of Defense memo signed 2026-09-22 and released 2026-09-28 directs Cyber Command, NSA, DIA and NGA to counter foreign threats to the 2026 elections, with Cyber Command using its existing authorities, and to coordinate with DHS, which runs opposite to the recommendation. Earlier, CNN reported on 2026-04-30 that the joint NSA and Cyber Command Election Security Group, which had operated for each general and midterm election since 2020, had not yet been activated for the 2026 midterms, and the commander told a Senate hearing he did not know whether one had been established but was prepared to set one up. On offensive operations, the national cyber strategy released 2026-03-06 commits to using offensive as well as defensive cyber capabilities against adversaries without naming DOD or Cyber Command, and EO 14390 of the same date has the Secretary of War support efforts to disrupt malicious cyber actors. Activity under NSPM-13, which the Mandate ties to defensive operations, is classified.

timeline.event: White House releases the national cyber strategy, whose first pillar commits to using defensive and offensive cyber capabilities against adversaries.
EO 14390 signed: the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security, supported by the Secretary of War, to enhance attribution, tracking and disruption of malicious cyber actors.
CNN reports the NSA and Cyber Command Election Security Group, used for each general and midterm election since 2020, had not been activated for the 2026 midterms.
Secretary of Defense memo directs Cyber Command, NSA, DIA and NGA to counter foreign threats to the 2026 elections and coordinate with DHS (released 2026-09-28).

Offensive and defensive cyber-effects activity, including under NSPM-13, is classified and was not verifiable.
